geometry_edits.rationale: Align the carved access response with the verified access side.
Broaden the access carve to strengthen public legibility at grade.
Increase the vertical reach of the notch so the void participates in section, not only plan.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the public relief aligned to the verified access side so the ground threshold reads intentionally open.
Widen the entry cut slightly so the access edge becomes a more legible public seam rather than a thin incision.
Extend the notch vertically to better register the public threshold in section and improve programmatic ground openness.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage neighborhood massing: one dominant compact bar-like body is still legible across all four views, and the top/front/isometric views agree enough to avoid a one-view-only form. The split and notch operations give the building a usable public seam, especially relative to the verified access edge, and the mass is not just a generic box. That said, the void is still somewhat shallow and the section remains close to a stacked extrusion rather than a more expressive active-ground / calm-upper composition. Because the program is neighborhood living, the visible mass is plausible, but it would benefit from a cleaner access-side carve or courtyard emphasis and a slightly stronger section logic toward public threshold rather than pure object-making.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more sculptural and curved than the candidate; avoid copying the scalloped roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact pavilion-like massing with a large carved void and an upper connector/bridge can create a clear public threshold without losing a dominant body.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a larger multi-building composition; candidate should not expand into campus sprawl.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation around a central plaza can support neighborhood living when the void is legible and the masses remain hierarchy-driven.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and glazed; candidate is heavier and more opaque.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low, spread-out mass with a courtyard and folded roof can keep the ground active while preserving a calm horizontal profile.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference leans more clearly into terrace/ramp sequencing than the candidate currently does.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, winged masses connected around a shared open core can produce a strong neighborhood threshold and sectionally meaningful public space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more fragmented and complex; candidate should remain more compact and controlled.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with voids under elevated blocks can maintain hierarchy while giving the ground plane public relief.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the provided diagram, so no hard gate failure there.
The access-edge response is present but modest; it reads more as a notch seam than a robust public forecourt or undercut.
Sectional expression is only moderately programmatic; the roof/massing remains fairly flat and rectilinear compared with the stronger folded or terraced precedents.
